mono.$description: Code and anything that must line up character by character.

xs.$description: The floor: a caption or a helper line that must not compete with its subject.

lg.$description: Above body text, for a heading that groups rather than announces.

xl.$description: A section title above the content it introduces.

2xl.$description: A page title: the largest size the scale offers.

regular.$description: Body text, and any label that is not deliberately stronger.

semibold.$description: Headings and labels that must hold their own against body text.

bold.$description: Emphasis inside a sentence: what `strong` and `b` already render, and the only weight the browser applies without asking.

tight.$description: Multi-line headings, where the lines belong to one phrase.

relaxed.$description: Long passages that are read rather than scanned.

tight.$description: Large sizes set slightly closer, because type opens up as it grows.

normal.$description: The absence of tracking: what a size needs unless it opts out.

heading-lg.$description: A page title. One per page.

heading-md.$description: A section title above the content it introduces.

heading-sm.$description: The smallest heading: it groups, it does not announce.

body-sm.$description: Running text in a dense surface: a table cell, a description.

label-md.$description: The label of a control: short, and never a sentence.
